content: Neosporin is the brand name of an antibiotic ointment originally produced by Pfizer and later sold to Johnson & Johnson. It is primarily used to prevent infections and promote the healing of wounds. The original formulation of Neosporin contains three antibiotics: bacitracin, neomycin, and polymyxin B. These antibiotics work synergistically to target a broad spectrum of bacteria. Specifically, neomycin and polymyxin B are effective against gram-negative bacteria, while bacitracin is active against gram-positive bacteria. This combination, often referred to as a triple antibiotic ointment, provides comprehensive coverage against bacterial infections in wounds. However, these antibiotics are generally limited to topical use due to the risk of severe systemic side effects, such as nephrotoxicity, when administered parenterally. Even with topical application, side effects can occur. Neomycin, in particular, is known to cause allergic reactions, including allergic contact dermatitis. Additionally, while Neosporin is effective, it is known to sometimes intensify the pain associated with abrasions and external injuries, though this effect is typically harmless. Neosporin is also marketed under other brand names, such as Mycitracin and Topisporin. Pfizer produces a related product called Polysporin, which contains only bacitracin and polymyxin B, omitting neomycin. This makes Polysporin a safer alternative for individuals with neomycin allergies. Pfizer has also introduced a product called Neosporin + Pain Relief, which includes pramoxine, a topical analgesic. This formulation is available as both an ointment and a cream. The cream version excludes bacitracin zinc, as it is unstable in the cream base, making it suitable for individuals sensitive to bacitracin or zinc. In Canada, the Neosporin brand is not available. Instead, Polysporin is sold in various formulations. The original Polysporin ointments contain polymyxin B and bacitracin, while the creams and eye/ear drops include polymyxin B and gramicidin. Additionally, a triple antibiotic ointment is available in Canada, which includes all three antibiotics: bacitracin, neomycin, and polymyxin B.
